q: 1. The maximum permissible eccentricity of load on a rectangular foundation with width B is equal to ---
explain: According to the 'Middle Third Rule,' to avoid tension in the base of a foundation, the eccentricity (e) must not exceed B/6.

q: 2. A foundation could fail due to ..........
options: unequal distribution of weight of the structure
horizontal movement of earth adjoining the structure
explain: Foundations fail when the soil's bearing capacity is exceeded, when the soil moves laterally, or when differential settlement creates internal stresses.

q: 3. The safe bearing capacity under dynamic loads such as machine foundations is taken to be...
options: more than that for static loads
same as that for static loads
less than that for static loads
depends on the weight of machine
explain: Dynamic/vibratory loads can cause soil liquefaction or additional settlement, so the allowable bearing capacity is reduced (often by 25-50%) compared to static loads.

q: 4. To improve the bearing capacity of the foundation, the cement grouting may be used if the foundation consists of .........
explain: Cement grouting is effective in rocks or coarse gravels where the grout can flow into fissures and voids to create a monolithic, stronger mass.

q: 5. If the soil is water logged, its bearing capacity may be improved by .........
explain: Water logging increases pore water pressure and reduces effective stress; removing the water through drainage significantly restores soil strength.

q: 6. A footing which supports two columns is known as .........
explain: A combined footing is a single foundation slab that carries the load of two or more columns, usually used when columns are close together.

q: 7. If footing supports more than two columns, it is called .........
explain: A continuous footing supports a long wall or a row of three or more columns in a line.

q: 8. The safe bearing capacity of medium clay which can be readily intended with a thumb nail is taken as ............
explain: Soil consistency can be field-tested by hand; medium clay, which is moderately firm, typically has a bearing capacity around 25 t/m².

q: 9. The thickness of staining in well foundations is generally about (where D is the diameter of the well)
explain: Staining (the wall of the well) must be thick enough to resist external earth/water pressure; D/4 is a common empirical ratio for design.

q: 10. The tilt in the well foundations should not exceed .........
explain: During the sinking of caissons/wells, the vertical alignment (tilt) is strictly monitored and should not deviate more than 1 in 200.

q: 11. The piles used in the construction of coffer dams .........
explain: Coffer dams are temporary water-tight structures; sheet piles are used to create the walls that hold back the water.

q: 12. The pile used to resist large horizontal or inclined force is ...........
explain: Batten (or Batter) piles are driven at an angle (inclined) to resist lateral forces from wind, water, or earth pressure.

q: 13. The foundation in which a cantilever beam is provided to join two footings, is known as
explain: A strap footing uses a cantilever 'strap' beam to connect an eccentric exterior footing to an interior footing, balancing the overturning moment caused by the edge load.

q: 14. The types of foundation used to transfer heavy load is
explain: Grillage foundations consist of tiers of steel beams (I-sections) encased in concrete. They are used specifically to spread very heavy concentrated loads from columns over a large area.

q: 15. In case of foundation on black cotton soil, the most suitable method to improve the bearing capacity of soil
explain: Because black cotton soil is chemically unstable (swelling/shrinking), the most reliable method for light structures is replacing the top 1-2 meters of soil with a non-expansive material like sand or moorum.

q: 16. In rectangular foundation of which 'B' the maximum permissible eccentricity of load is limited to
explain: To ensure no tension develops at the base of a foundation (the 'middle-third' rule), the eccentricity 'e' must not exceed B/6 for rectangular bases.

q: 17. Width of wall footing (according to thumb's rule) is
explain: A common rule of thumb for footing width is twice the wall thickness plus 30 cm (2t + 300mm) to ensure proper load distribution to the soil.

q: 18. Which type of foundation is likely to be adopted for a 3 storey RCC framed building?
explain: For a standard 3-story framed building with good soil, isolated footings under each column are the most common and economical choice.

q: 19. An arrangement supporting an existing structure by providing supports underneath is known as ........
explain: Underpinning is the process of strengthening or deepening the foundation of an existing building by adding supports underneath.

q: 20. A plate load test is useful to determine
explain: The plate load test provides data on both the ultimate bearing capacity of the soil and the anticipated settlement under load.

q: 21. The maximum total settlement for raft foundation on clayey soils is usually limited to
explain: For clayey soils, raft foundations are generally designed to limit total settlement to 65-100 mm.

q: 22. The maximum total settlement for raft foundation on sand is usually limited to
explain: Settlement in sand occurs more rapidly and is typically capped at 40-65 mm for raft foundations.

q: 23. The maximum differential settlement in case of foundation on clayey soils is usually limited to
explain: To prevent structural damage in clay, differential settlement (difference in settlement between two points) is limited to 40 mm.

q: 24. The maximum differential settlement, in case of foundation on sandy soils is usually limited to
explain: In sandy soils, the allowable differential settlement is stricter, usually limited to 25 mm.

q: 25. The maximum total settlement for isolated foundation on clayey soils should be limited to
explain: Isolated footings on clay are typically permitted a total settlement of up to 65 mm.

q: 26. Raft foundation are generally preferred to when the area required for individual footing is more than
explain: When individual footings cover more than 50% of the building area, a continuous raft (mat) becomes more economical and better at preventing differential settlement.

q: 27. Pile foundation is generally provided if soil is
explain: Piles are deep foundations used when surface soil is weak, highly compressible, or waterlogged, transferring the load to deeper, more stable strata.

q: 28. Safe bearing capacity of Black cotton soil varies from
explain: Black cotton soil is notoriously unstable due to high swelling and shrinkage; its safe bearing capacity is very low, typically 5 to 7.5 t/m².

q: 29. The process of finding out the soil strata below ground level is known as
explain: Subsoil exploration involves boring and sampling to determine the engineering properties and layers of the soil before construction.

q: 30. The highest point on the extrados of the arch is known as ..........
explain: The crown is the highest part or apex of the arch's exterior curve.

q: 31. The arrangement of supporting an existing structure by providing supports underneath is known as
explain: Underpinning is the method used to strengthen or deepen the foundation of an existing building or structure.

q: 32. A group of tapering steps radiating from same point is known as ..........
explain: Winders are steps that are narrower at one end than the other, used to change the direction of the stairs.

q: 33. The building of an Engineering college should be classified as
explain: Buildings used for instructional purposes are classified as Educational buildings.

q: 34. The load of furniture stored in a building is termed as
explain: Live loads (imposed loads) are movable loads, such as people, furniture, and movable equipment.

q: 35. While calculating the dead load of a building, the weight of brick masonry is taken as
explain: The unit weight of common brick masonry is standardly taken as 19.2 kN/m³ (approx 1920 Kg/m³).

q: 36. The safe bearing capacity for hard rock should be
explain: Hard, massive rock has very high bearing capacity, typically exceeding 250 t/m² (2500 kN/m²).

q: 37. Generally for a column in a workshop using Gantry cranes, the foundation to be used should be
explain: Grillage foundations are used for heavy isolated column loads to spread the pressure over a larger area of soil.

q: 38. For an ordinary double storey building, the type of foundation to be used should be
explain: Spread footings are the most common and economical choice for low-rise residential structures on stable soil.

q: 39. While constructing a bridge upon a river, the foundation to be adopted in pillars should be
explain: Well (Caisson) foundations are standard for bridge piers in rivers due to their ability to withstand scour and provide high load capacity.

q: 40. For a bridge pier, in very deep water the foundation to be used should be
explain: In very deep water where a standard well foundation is difficult, a pneumatic or floating caisson is used.

q: 41. Lift becomes essential in building when the number of floors exceeds ..........
explain: In standard building bylaws, a lift is generally required when a building is G+3 (4 floors) or higher to ensure accessibility.

q: 42. Ventilation means ..........
options: replacing the impure air in the building by fresh air from outside
explain: The fundamental purpose of ventilation is the continuous supply of fresh outdoor air and the removal of contaminated indoor air.

q: 43. Which of the following has the lowest bearing capacity?
explain: Soft clay has very low shear strength and high compressibility, giving it one of the lowest safe bearing capacities.

q: 44. Which of the following has the highest bearing capacity?
explain: Hard igneous rocks like granite or basalt have extremely high bearing capacities, often exceeding 3000 kN/m2.

q: 45. Black cotton soil is often termed as treacherous soil. The reason being ..........
explain: Black cotton soil contains montmorillonite clay which expands and contracts violently with moisture changes, causing foundation failure.

q: 46. The black cotton soil is unsuitable for foundations because
options: it is difficult to excavate it
explain: Black cotton soil has a low bearing capacity and is highly susceptible to volumetric changes (swelling and shrinking) due to moisture variations.

q: 47. Codes used in Nepal for building construction/ design is
explain: Nepal follows its own National Building Code (NBC) for structural design and safety.

q: 48. Raft foundations are preferred when the area required for all the individual footings is more than ........
explain: When individual footings cover more than 50% of the total building area, a raft (or mat) foundation becomes more economical and effective.

q: 49. The foundations are placed below ground level, to increase
explain: Embedding foundations below ground level provides lateral support and prevents sliding, increasing stability.

q: 50. The type of steel pile which is generally sunk in soft clay and loose sand of low bearing capacity is ........
explain: Screw piles consist of a hollow shaft with a screw-like blade at the bottom, making them ideal for soft clays and loose sands.
